turns.text: In your aiseasonlead-mid-task repository, specifically in app.py, you implemented a Flask server that runs an agent in a background thread and streams logs via Server-Sent Events. Could you explain your approach to managing thread safety and handling memory or job state cleanup via the _prune_jobs function in a production environment?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Um, sorry, let me think about this properly -- so, the jobs dict is shared across the request thread and the background thread, so I put a lock around any write to it. _prune_jobs runs periodically and just... it removes entries past a TTL. I'm not totally sure that's the most elegant way to do it, but that's the reasoning.

Playwright can be notoriously fragile due to network delays and dynamic page rendering. How did you handle error recovery, session timeouts, and parsing reliability when the DOM structure changed unexpectedly?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Playwright kept timing out on slow-loading pages, so I wrapped the selector waits in a retry with a timeout, and if the page structure changed I'd fall back to searching by text instead of the exact selector. I'm not 100% sure I handled every edge case, some scrapes probably still failed silently, but the retry logic caught most of it.

turns.speaker: candidate
